pole_a.label: craft
sentences: We take the time to get the details right, even when no one would notice.
We build things meant to still work beautifully in ten years.
Every part of the product reflects the care of the person who made it.
We'd rather do fewer things at an exceptional standard than many things adequately.
Quality is never traded away to hit a date.
Polish is a form of respect for the user, so we sweat the details.
Durability matters here: we design and build for the long run.
Craftsmanship guides everything we make, from the first sketch to the final release.

pole_b.label: iteration
sentences: We release small changes continuously and let real usage tell us what to fix.
A shipped experiment teaches us more than a month of planning.
Our first version is never our best version — that's by design.
We treat every launch as a draft we will keep improving.
We'd rather put something rough in front of users today than something polished next quarter.
Learning quickly matters more to us than getting it right the first time.
We iterate in public, shipping improvements every week instead of saving them for a big release.
Perfect is a moving target, so we optimize for feedback loops instead.
